````text
---
name: task-group-completeness
description: Perform a deep engineering completeness review of proposed task groups against the full stack, complete specs, data model, runtime state, and operator constraints. Repair the injected input card when fundamental tasks are missing, then write the injected report card. Use after task-dependency and before implementation-orchestrator launches workers.
---

## A. Purpose

1. This skill performs a **deep engineering completeness review** of **proposed task groups** before **implementation worker dispatch**.
2. It judges whether the plan is **logically solid**, **technically complete**, and grounded in the **full stack**, **complete specs**, **data model**, **runtime state**, and **operator constraints**.
3. It returns `ready` only when no **fundamental implementation tasks** are missing, and `blocked` when **planning logic** has unresolved gaps.

---

## B. Deep Planning Audit

1. Reconstruct the **implementation logic** from the injected source material, not just the **task list**.
2. Judge whether the grouped plan would produce a **coherent implementation** across **architecture**, **data**, **state**, **APIs**, **UI**, **config**, **migrations**, **tests**, **fixtures**, and **handoff**.
3. Look for **fundamental missing tasks** that would make implementation fail even when every requirement appears mapped and every task appears grouped.
4. Treat traceability checks as **supporting evidence**, not the **audit result**.
5. Reject a plan that is only **performatively complete**: named tasks, mapped requirements, and grouped work are not enough to prove **engineering completeness**.

---

## C. Input Card Changes

1. Repair the injected **input card** before writing the **report card** when deep analysis finds a **fundamental task gap**.
2. Add missing tasks needed for **architecture boundaries**, **data model changes**, **state transitions**, **API contracts**, **UI behavior**, **config changes**, **migrations**, **fixtures**, **test strategy**, and **handoff data**.
3. Amend **existing groups** when they hide **dependencies**, **sequencing risks**, **shared-file collisions**, **missing integration work**, **missing verification strategy**, and **unclear implementation ownership**.
4. Leave a **blocking question** only when the full stack and spec evidence does not determine the **necessary task**.
5. Keep the edited card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## D. Report Card

1. Write the **audit report** into the injected **report card** after the **input card changes** are complete.
2. The report card explains the **engineering reasoning**, the **planning risks tested**, the **input card repairs**, the **remaining gaps**, and the final **dispatch decision**.
3. Include the **report sections** `Engineering Completeness Findings`, `Fundamental Missing Tasks`, `Input Card Edits Applied`, `Dispatch-Ready Groups`, `Blocking Questions`, and `Dispatch Readiness`.
4. Include **group ids**, **task ids**, **source card ids**, **target files**, **missing engineering logic**, **verification strategy**, **migration needs**, **fixture needs**, **config needs**, **unanswered questions**, and final status using `ready` and `blocked`.
5. Keep the report card in the **same structure and style** as this skill.

---

## E. Hard Rules

1. Do not approve a **group** from **checkbox traceability** without testing the **engineering logic** behind the plan.
2. Do not invent **tasks** without **source evidence**.
3. Do not treat **requirement-to-task mapping** and **task-to-group mapping** as proof of **planning completeness**.
4. Do not leave an **input-card correction** only in the **report card**.
5. Use bold only for the **important words that carry the point** inside a sentence; do not turn each **numbered item opening** into a subtitle.
6. Do not implement **product code** and do not run **implementation tests**.
7. Do not change **card status** during this audit.
````

.decision-os/runs/codex-skills/tasks-system/codex-skill-1783595913386-e48acfb6.jsonl:5:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/zsh -lc \"sed -n '1,240p' /home/jbb/.codex/skills/task-dependency/SKILL.md && rg --files /home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os | rg '(\"'^|/)(shared/schemas|backend/src/business/codex|backend/src/business/server/helper/create-http-server.ts|backend/src/business/ledger/helper/card-content-file.ts|frontend/src/runtime/codex|frontend/src/runtime/input/controller/handle-action-click.ts|frontend/src/runtime/canvas/effect/render-canvas-control-overlay.ts|frontend/src/runtime/dom.ts|frontend/index.html|frontend/assets/canvas/(dialogs|objects)'\"\\\\.css|tests/browser/codex|backend/test/codex|frontend/test/runtime)'\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: task-dependency\ndescription: Analyze a `task-list` inventory and create dependency edges, independent implementation groups, sequential gates, collision risks, and readiness for `task-group-completeness`. Use after `task-list` returns `READY_FOR_TASK_DEPENDENCY` and before implementation grouping is audited.\n---\n\n# Task Dependency\n\n## A. Scope\n\n1. **Purpose.** Convert the flat `task-list` inventory into a dependency graph and implementation groups that can be worked independently where the evidence supports it.\n2. **Start point.** Use this skill only after the upstream `task-list` output includes `Task Inventory`, `Open Questions`, and `Readiness`.\n3. **Readiness gate.** Continue only when the upstream readiness value is `READY_FOR_TASK_DEPENDENCY`.\n4. **Stop point.** Do not implement tasks, run tests, judge group completeness, or dispatch implementation workers.\n\n---\n\n## B. Required Inputs\n\n1. **Task inventory.** Read the complete `task-list` output, including every `id`, `type`, `title`, `target_files`, `target_symbols`, `action`, `done_when`, and `depends_on` value.\n2. **Source material.** Read any source cards, specs, architecture notes, codebase surface maps, data model notes, runtime state notes, migration notes, fixture notes, and test strategy included with the run.\n3. **Codebase evidence.** Inspect the codebase only as needed to verify dependency evidence, shared ownership, file-family collisions, runtime-state coupling, migration order, and test fixture order.\n\n---\n\n## C. Dependency Construction\n\n1. **Seed explicit edges.** Treat each populated `depends_on` value from `task-list` as an explicit dependency edge before inferring additional edges.\n2. **Infer required edges.** Add an inferred edge only when file ownership, symbol ownership, data flow, runtime state, migration order, fixture setup, API contract order, or test setup proves that one task must happen before another task.\n3. **Classify every edge.** Use exactly one edge type: `hard-blocker`, `shared-file-risk`, `shared-state-risk`, `test-order-risk`, `migration-order-risk`, or `soft-ordering`.\n4. **Ground every edge.** Record the concrete evidence for each edge from task fields, source material, file paths, symbols, migrations, fixtures, tests, or runtime state.\n5. **Preserve uncertainty.** Put unclear relationships in `Ambiguities` instead of forcing a dependency edge or an implementation group.\n\n---\n\n## D. Group Construction\n\n1. **Place every task.** Put every task in exactly one proposed implementation group unless the task is explicitly blocked by an ambiguity.\n2. **Keep collision-prone work together.** Keep tasks in the same group when splitting them would force multiple workers to edit the same file family, state object, migration chain, fixture, scenario setup, or test harness.\n3. **Separate independent work.** Split tasks into separate groups only when their target files, target symbols, tests, fixtures, runtime state, and data assumptions can be changed independently.\n4. **Respect gates.** Preserve sequential gates between groups when one group creates an API, schema, migration, fixture, state contract, or shared behavior that another group consumes.\n5. **Avoid fake parallelism.** Do not optimize for maximum group count when shared-file conflicts would make parallel work unsafe.\n\n---\n\n## E. Output Contract\n\n1. **`Dependency Graph`.** Produce a table with `from_task`, `to_task`, `edge_type`, `reason`, and `evidence`.\n2. **`Independent Task Groups`.** Produce a table with `group_id`, `task_ids`, `target_files`, `target_symbols`, `independence_reason`, and `dispatch_notes`.\n3. **`Sequential Gates`.** List group-to-group gates with the required completion condition for each downstream group.\n4. **`Collision Risks`.** List files, symbols, tests, fixtures, migrations, data models, and runtime state that make parallel work unsafe.\n5. **`Ambiguities`.** List only dependency questions that block reliable grouping.\n6. **`Readiness`.** End with exactly one readiness value. Use `READY_FOR_TASK_GROUP_COMPLETENESS` when grouping is reliable. Use `BLOCKED_NEEDS_OPERATOR_ANSWER` when an operator answer is required.\n\n---\n\n## F. Hard Rules\n\n1. **No implementation.** Do not edit product code, tests, fixtures, migrations, config, or docs while using this skill.\n2. **No test runs.** Do not run verification commands while creating the dependency graph.\n3. **No invented tasks.** Do not create implementation tasks; report missing or unsafe work as an ambiguity for the next gate.\n4. **No hidden blockers.** Do not put an '');\n  }\n  return '';\n}\n\nasync function resizeChangedCardToContent(contentFile: string): Promise<void> {\n  const cardId = changedCardIdForContentFile(contentFile);\n  if (!cardId) {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize-skipped', { reason: 'card-not-found', contentFile });\n    return;\n  }\n  const geometry = resizeSelectedCardsToContent({ cardIds: [cardId], zoneIds: [] });\n  if (Object.keys(geometry.cards).length === 0 && Object.keys(geometry.zones).length === 0) {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize-skipped', { reason: 'empty-geometry', contentFile, cardId });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  persistState();\n  const committed = state.activeLedger\n    ? await commitActiveLedgerMutation({ action: 'patch-geometry', geometry }, { render: true })\n    : false;\n  telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize', { contentFile, cardId, committed });\n}\n\nasync function reloadLedgerContent(reason: string, options: LedgerRefreshOptions = {}): Promise<void> {\n  if (refreshInFlight) {\n    state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = true;\n    return;\n  }\n  refreshInFlight = true;\n  try {\n    await loadActiveLedgerState();\n    renderCanvasSurface();\n    if (options.contentFile) await resizeChangedCardToContent(options.contentFile);\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh', { reason, contentFile: options.contentFile ?? '' });\n  } finally {\n    refreshInFlight = false;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function reloadThreadContent(reason: string): Promise<void> {\n  if (threadRefreshInFlight) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = true;\n    return;\n  }\n  threadRefreshInFlight = true;\n  const selection = state.selection;\n  try {\n    await loadActiveLedgerState();\n    state.selection = options);\n}\n\nexport function requestThreadContentRefresh(reason = 'thread-content-change'): void {\n  if (state.voice?.recording) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = true;\n state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = false;\n    void reloadLedgerContent(reason);\n  }\n  if (state.pendingThreadContentRefresh) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = false;\n    void });\n  events.addEventListener('ledger-content-change', (event) => {\n    const payload = contentEventPayload(event);\n    maybeResumeCodexRunWidget(payload);\n    requestLedgerContentRefresh(payload.reason || 'ledger-content-change');\n  });\n  events.onerror = () => {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-stream-error', {});\n  };\n .decision-os/backups/card-content-file-20260529-173834/specs.json:5273:        "what": "Card-to-zone attribution and derived readable zone colors must be cached from ledger/canvas geometry instead of recomputed during pan, zoom, selection rendering, or full surface refreshes that do not change geometry. The cache key is the active ledger tab plus card and regular-zone geometry/color revision. It stores each card id's owning regular zone id, raw zone color, readable/clamped color, and fallback/no-zone state. The cache is invalidated only when a card or regular zone is created, deleted, moved, resized, recolored, or when a new ledger tab is loaded; viewport pan/zoom, low-detail mode changes, relationship redraw, selection changes, thread panel changes, and telemetry rendering must not invalidate or recompute attribution.\n\nRefactor shape: introduce a canvas runtime `zoneAttributionCache` owned outside the DOM renderer. Build it from `state.activeLedger.cards` and regular `annotations` using ledger coordinates on ledger load/render, and update dirty entries incrementally from geometry mutation paths. `patchLedgerCard()` applies cached `data-card-zone-id`, `data-card-zone-color`, `--card-zone-color`, `--card-code-color`, and `--card-readable-color` without measuring DOM. `renderCardZoneColors()` becomes a fallback/compatibility effect for static non-ledger cards and explicit dirty-zone recalculation only; it must not scan every card against every zone during pan or zoom. Acceptance: a synthetic 15-zone x 5-card-per-zone canvas must keep plain pan pointermove transform-only, pan pointerup under 16 ms when no geometry changed, and 10-15 wheel zoom events must not trigger card-zone attribution recomputation."

.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:5:3. **Primary failure class.** The existing fixes protect server refresh merge results for geometry and viewport values, but they do not protect the active interaction session that connects `state.pointer.targetId`, `state.selection`, `state.viewport`, rendered DOM nodes, and `patch-geometry` payloads.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:6:4. **In-scope runtime paths.** The affected files are `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-active-ledger-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/controller/refresh-runtime-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/effect/subscribe-ledger-content-events.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-down.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-move.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-up.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/selection/effect/move-selected.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/commit-selected-ledger-geometry.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/active-ledger-geometry.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/card/effect/resize-selected-card.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/zone/effect/resize-selected-zone.ts`.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:13:2. **Manual refresh clears selection twice.** `refreshRuntimeState()` preserves the local viewport for the next ledger id, reads persisted state, clears `state.selection`, hydrates persisted geometry, then calls `loadActiveLedgerState()`, which clears `state.selection` again.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:14:3. **Ledger content refresh remounts canvas state.** `reloadLedgerContent()` calls `loadActiveLedgerState()`, calls `renderCanvasSurface()`, and optionally resizes the changed card with `resizeChangedCardToContent()`. It does not capture the active pointer session and does not preserve current selection explicitly.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:15:4. **Thread content refresh can restore stale selection.** `reloadThreadContent()` captures `const selection = state.selection`, awaits `loadActiveLedgerState()`, then assigns `state.selection = selection`. If the operator changes selection while the fetch is in flight, the old snapshot can overwrite the newer selection.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:25:1. **`bed5d24` - Preserve local canvas state during ledger refresh.** This commit added `mergeLocalCanvasStateIntoLedger()`, added `state.activeLedgerId`, preserved local card, zone, and group geometry by id during same-ledger refresh, and preserved the current viewport during same-ledger refresh. Its tests cover same-ledger geometry plus viewport preservation and non-geometry mutation responses. It did not protect `state.selection`, active pointer identity, active drag target identity, active pan session state, and refreshes that complete after the viewport changes while fetch is in flight.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:27:3. **`e1a55b5` - Keep current viewport during ledger refresh.** This commit moved the same-ledger viewport snapshot in `loadActiveLedgerState()` to after the fetch and JSON parse, then added a test where `state.viewport.x`, `state.viewport.y`, and `state.viewport.scale` change while the server load is in flight. It covers viewport values during `loadActiveLedgerState()`. It does not cover active pointer pan continuity, wheel persistence timer freshness, selection continuity, and drag identity continuity.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:28:4. **`88856a3` - Preserve multi-selection on drag start.** This adjacent commit protects the initial drag selection rules through `selectionIncludesTarget()`. It does not protect the selection after refresh code mutates `state.selection`.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:37:1. **Selection rollback.** `loadActiveLedgerState()` and `refreshRuntimeState()` still clear `state.selection`. `reloadThreadContent()` still restores a pre-refresh selection snapshot after an async ledger load. The result can be empty selection, older selection, and newer operator selection being overwritten.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:38:2. **Wrong drag target.** `handlePointerDown()` records the intended target in `state.pointer.targetId`, but drag movement and geometry commit use live `state.selection`. A refresh between pointer down and pointer move can make `moveSelected()` move the wrong card, zone, group, and attached selection set.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:39:3. **Wrong geometry payload.** A refresh between pointer move and pointer up can make `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` commit geometry for the current `state.selection`, not the selected ids that belonged to the pointer session.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:50:2. **Async refresh writes global state after awaits.** `loadActiveLedgerState()`, `reloadLedgerContent()`, `reloadThreadContent()`, and `refreshRuntimeState()` write selection and active ledger state after network and file-refresh awaits without checking whether a pointer session started, moved, changed selection, and reached release during the wait.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:58:1. **Capture a pointer selection snapshot.** After `handlePointerDown()` finishes `selectTarget()` for `drag`, `group`, and `resize`, store `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` with `cardIds`, `zoneIds`, `groupIds`, `targetKind`, `targetId`, and the current `ledgerStateId`.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:59:2. **Move explicit gesture selection.** Update `moveSelected()` to accept an explicit selection argument and use that selection for ledger geometry mutation, DOM position patches, telemetry, zone labels, relationship overlays, and canvas controls. `handlePointerMove()` must pass `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` for active drag and group gestures.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:60:3. **Commit explicit gesture selection.** Update `commitSelectedLedgerGeometry()` to accept an explicit selection argument and pass that selection to `selectedLedgerGeometryPayload(selection)`. `handlePointerUp()` must commit `pointerSession.selectionSnapshot` for drag, group, and resize releases.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:62:5. **Preserve same-ledger selection through refresh.** Update `loadActiveLedgerState()` so same-ledger refresh keeps the current selection after pruning selected ids that no longer exist in the refreshed ledger. Route changes and ledger changes remain the only paths that clear selection.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:63:6. **Protect active pointer selection during refresh.** When `state.pointer` is active, refresh code must keep `state.pointer.selectionSnapshot` unchanged and must restore visible `state.selection` from that snapshot after the active ledger merge finishes.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:64:7. **Prevent stale thread refresh selection restore.** Update `reloadThreadContent()` so it restores the captured selection only when no pointer session is active and the visible selection has not changed since the snapshot was captured. If selection changed during the await, the newer selection remains authoritative.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:74:4. **Thread refresh selection freshness.** If `reloadThreadContent()` starts with `card-a` selected and the operator selects `card-b` before the load resolves, the final visible selection must stay on `card-b`.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:85:2. **Thread refresh race test.** Extend `frontend/test/runtime/ledger-content-refresh.integration.test.ts` with an async `requestThreadContentRefresh()` case that changes selection before the load resolves and verifies the newer selection wins.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:98:3. **Current runtime sources.** `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/load-active-ledger-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/commit-active-ledger-mutation.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/merge-local-canvas-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/controller/refresh-runtime-state.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/refresh/effect/subscribe-ledger-content-events.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-down.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-move.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-pointer-up.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/gesture/controller/handle-wheel.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/selection/effect/move-selected.ts`, `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/effect/commit-selected-ledger-geometry.ts`, and `frontend/src/runtime/ledger/helper/active-ledger-geometry.ts`.
.decision-os/cards/bugs/card-0b1aed1f-c9f5-4154-ab9a-a26058426b5c.md:99:4. **Current test sources.** `frontend/test/runtime/active-ledger-zone-lifecycle.integration.test.ts`, `frontend/test/runtime/ledger-content-refresh.integration.test.ts`, `frontend/test/runtime/selection-direct-card-click.integration.test.ts`, `frontend/test/runtime/canvas-pan-performance.integration.test.ts`, `frontend/test/runtime/drag-release-freeze.integration.test.ts`, `frontend/test/refresh/client-refresh.integration.test.ts`, and `tests/browser/refresh/the-refresh-system-preserves-canvas-continuity-during-operator-work.spec.ts`.

.decision-os/runs/codex-skills/tasks-system/codex-skill-1783591708289-5fd90c7c.jsonl:5:{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_1","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/zsh -lc \"pwd && sed -n '1,240p' /home/jbb/.codex/skills/task-list/SKILL.md\"","aggregated_output":"/home/jbb/dev/EditorBP/decision-os\n---\nname: task-list\ndescription: Create concise, codebase-grounded task inventories from a clarified Decision OS source card and any run-provided source material. Use after expected behavior is clear and before dependency grouping, orchestration, implementation, or test attribution needs actionable tasks linked to files, symbols, task type, and completion checks.\n---\n\n# Task List\n\n## A. Scope\n\n1. **Purpose.** Convert clarified planning material into an actionable task inventory that an engineer or implementation agent can execute without rediscovering the problem.\n2. **Start point.** Use this skill only after the operator intent, constraints, and expected behavior are clear enough to split work.\n3. **Stop point.** Do not group dependencies, dispatch workers, implement code, run tests, or perform test attribution.\n\n---\n\n## B. Required Inputs\n\n1. **Run source.** Read the source card path passed to the run.\n2. **No source filtering.** Do not ignore source material because its kind is not named in this skill.\n3. **Codebase grounding.** Inspect the codebase enough to link tasks to real files and symbols.\n\n---\n\n## C. Task Construction\n\n1. **Extract work.** Capture each required behavior change, UI change, data change, test need, fixture, config change, doc change, operation, discovery step, and operator decision.\n2. **Discover targets.** Do the additional codebase discovery needed to name target files and symbols before writing the task list.\n3. **Create tasks.** Make each task an actionable codebase-linked change, not a research placeholder.\n4. **Choose type.** Let the model choose the shortest useful `type`. Common terms include `code`, `test`, `scenario`, `data`, `fixture`, `config`, `docs`, and `ops`, but this list is not exhaustive.\n5. **Define completion.** Give every task a concrete `done_when` check that is visible in code review, test output, rendered UI, data state, config, docs, or an operator answer.\n6. **Check coverage.** Confirm the task list covers the requested work or state the blocking question.\n\n---\n\n## D. Type Nomenclature\n\n1. **`code`.** Source behavior, UI behavior, API behavior, state handling, or internal logic.\n2. **`test`.** Automated verification: unit, integration, end-to-end, regression, or harness work.\n3. **`scenario`.** Human-readable behavior path that must be implemented or verified.\n4. **`data`.** Schema, migration, seed, backfill, persisted shape, or data contract work.\n5. **`fixture`.** Test data, mocks, stubs, snapshots, or repeatable setup data.\n6. **`config`.** Environment, build, package, CI, deploy, flag, or tool configuration.\n7. **`docs`.** Required developer, operator, or user-facing documentation.\n8. **`ops`.** Deploy, monitoring, rollback, manual operation, or release task.\n\n---\n\n## E. Output Contract\n\n1. **`Task Inventory`.** Produce one table with `id`, `type`, `title`, `target_files`, `target_symbols`, `action`, `done_when`, and `depends_on`.\n2. **`Open Questions`.** List only operator answers that block a reliable codebase-linked task list.\n3. **`Readiness`.** End with `READY_FOR_TASK_DEPENDENCY` or `BLOCKED_NEEDS_OPERATOR_ANSWER`.\n\n---\n\n## F. Hard Rules\n\n1. **No implementation.** Do not edit code.\n2. **No verification run.** Do not run tests.\n3. **No generic tasks.** Do not write tasks like `update backend`, `fix UI`, or `add tests` without a target or discovery action.\n4. **No invented requirements.** Do not add work that is not grounded in source material.\n5. **No fake targets.** If the file, symbol, or surface is unknown after discovery, ask a blocking question instead of guessing.\n6. **No report bloat.** Do not add rationale paragraphs, strategy essays, or duplicate sections.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

'');\n  try {\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(data) as Record<string, unknown>;\n    return {\n      cardId: typeof parsed.cardId === 'string' ? parsed.cardId : '',\n      contentFile: typeof parsed.contentFile === 'string' ? parsed.contentFile : '',\n      kind: typeof parsed.kind === 'string' ? parsed.kind : '',\n      ledgerId: typeof parsed.ledgerId === 'string' ? parsed.ledgerId : '',\n      outputCardId: typeof parsed.outputCardId === 'string' ? parsed.outputCardId : '',\n      reason: typeof parsed.reason === 'string' ? parsed.reason : '',\n      runId: typeof parsed.runId === 'string' ? parsed.runId : ''\n    };\n  } catch {\n    return {};\n  }\n}\n\nfunction maybeResumeCodexRunWidget(payload: ContentChangeEvent): void {\n  const reason = String(payload.reason ?? '');\n  if (!reason.startsWith('codex-') || !reason.endsWith('-started')) return;\n  const ledgerId = String(payload.ledgerId ?? '').trim();\n  const cardId = String(payload.outputCardId || payload.cardId || '').trim();\n  const runId = String(payload.runId ?? '').trim();\n  if (!ledgerId || !cardId || !runId) return;\n  resumeExternallyStartedCardSkillRun({ ledgerId, cardId, runId });\n}\n\nfunction normalizedContentFile(value: unknown): string {\n  const file = String(value ?? '').trim().replace(/\\\\/g, '/');\n  if (file.startsWith('/.decision-os/')) return file.slice(1);\n  return file.replace(/^\\.\\/+/, '');\n}\n\nexport function changedCardIdForContentFile(contentFile: string): string {\n  const target = normalizedContentFile(contentFile);\n  if (!target) return '';\n  const cards = Array.isArray(state.activeLedger?.cards) ? state.activeLedger.cards as Array<Record<string, unknown>> : [];\n  for (const card of cards) {\n    const comment = card.comment && typeof card.comment === 'object' ? card.comment as Record<string, unknown> : {};\n    if (normalizedContentFile(comment.contentFile) === target) return String(card.id ?? '');\n  }\n  return '';\n}\n\nasync function resizeChangedCardToContent(contentFile: string): Promise<void> {\n  const cardId = changedCardIdForContentFile(contentFile);\n  if (!cardId) {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize-skipped', { reason: 'card-not-found', contentFile });\n    return;\n  }\n  const geometry = resizeSelectedCardsToContent({ cardIds: [cardId], zoneIds: [] });\n  if (Object.keys(geometry.cards).length === 0 && Object.keys(geometry.zones).length === 0) {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize-skipped', { reason: 'empty-geometry', contentFile, cardId });\n    return;\n  }\n\n  persistState();\n  const committed = state.activeLedger\n    ? await commitActiveLedgerMutation({ action: 'patch-geometry', geometry }, { render: true })\n    : false;\n  telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-resize', { contentFile, cardId, committed });\n}\n\nasync function reloadLedgerContent(reason: string, options: LedgerRefreshOptions = {}): Promise<void> {\n  if (refreshInFlight) {\n    state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = true;\n    return;\n  }\n  refreshInFlight = true;\n  try {\n    await loadActiveLedgerState();\n    renderCanvasSurface();\n    if (options.contentFile) await resizeChangedCardToContent(options.contentFile);\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh', { reason, contentFile: options.contentFile ?? '' });\n  } finally {\n    refreshInFlight = false;\n  }\n}\n\nasync function reloadThreadContent(reason: string): Promise<void> {\n  if (threadRefreshInFlight) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = true;\n    return;\n  }\n  threadRefreshInFlight = true;\n  const selection = state.selection;\n  try {\n    await loadActiveLedgerState();\n    state.selection = selection;\n    renderThreadPanel();\n    telemetry('thread-content-refresh', { reason });\n  } finally {\n    threadRefreshInFlight = false;\n  }\n}\n\nexport function requestLedgerContentRefresh(reason = 'card-content-change', options: LedgerRefreshOptions = {}): void {\n  if (state.voice?.recording) {\n    state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = true;\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-deferred', { reason, voiceRecording: true });\n    return;\n  }\n  state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = false;\n  void reloadLedgerContent(reason, options);\n}\n\nexport function requestThreadContentRefresh(reason = 'thread-content-change'): void {\n  if (state.voice?.recording) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = true;\n    telemetry('thread-content-refresh-deferred', { reason, voiceRecording: true });\n    return;\n  }\n  state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = false;\n  void reloadThreadContent(reason);\n}\n\nexport function flushPendingLedgerContentRefresh(reason = 'voice-recording-stopped'): void {\n  if (state.voice?.recording) return;\n  if (state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh) {\n    state.pendingLedgerContentRefresh = false;\n    void reloadLedgerContent(reason);\n  }\n  if (state.pendingThreadContentRefresh) {\n    state.pendingThreadContentRefresh = false;\n    void reloadThreadContent(reason);\n  }\n}\n\nexport function subscribeLedgerContentEvents(): void {\n  if (subscribed || typeof EventSource === 'undefined') return;\n  subscribed = true;\n  const events = new EventSource('/api/ledger-content-events');\n  events.addEventListener('card-content-change', (event) => {\n    const payload = contentEventPayload(event);\n    if (payload.kind === 'thread-content') {\n      requestThreadContentRefresh('thread-content-change');\n      return;\n    }\n    requestLedgerContentRefresh('card-content-change', { contentFile: payload.contentFile });\n  });\n  events.addEventListener('ledger-content-change', (event) => {\n    const payload = contentEventPayload(event);\n    maybeResumeCodexRunWidget(payload);\n    requestLedgerContentRefresh(payload.reason || 'ledger-content-change');\n  });\n  events.onerror = () => {\n    telemetry('ledger-content-refresh-stream-error', {});\n  };\n  state.ledgerContentEventSource = events;\n  telemetry('subscribe-ledger-content-events', {});\n}\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Build/Debug Postmortem\\n\\n## Postmortem Summary\\n- The main debugging failures came from using the wrong telemetry source.\\n  - `frame_*.json` is useful for state snapshots, but not authoritative for phase/perf diagnosis.\\n  - Use GPU live debug events under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*` for pipeline diagnosis.\\n- Temporary scenario generation caused false conclusions.\\n  - The YAML parser expects inline arrays (`[x, y, z]`) for many fields.\\n  - Block-style arrays can silently fall back to defaults (notably `half_extents`, capture arrays).\\n- Runner return code is currently unreliable for success/failure classification.\\n  - `run-scenario.ps1` may return non-zero even when the simulation reaches final frame and writes captures.\\n  - Always validate with run artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n\\n## Correct Build Procedure\\n- Release (fast runtime checks):\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1`\\n- Debug + live debug pipeline:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug`\\n- Debug + live debug + GPU timing:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug -gpuTiming`\\n\\n## Correct Run Procedure\\n- Canonical scenario run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\\\" -Config Release`\\n- No-render stress run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"<scenario>.yaml\\\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\\n- Always check:\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\\n\\n## Legacy Output Caveat\\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\\n\\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\\n- Known transient symptom:\\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\\n- Retry policy:\\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \\\"Write-Output interop_ok\\\"`\\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\\n\\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\\n- Use event files first:\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\\n- For histograms/summaries:\\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\\n\\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\\n\\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\\n\\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\\n\\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\\n- Update incrementally with:\\n  - commands run\\n  - artifact paths\\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\\n  - test evidence\\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\\n  - integration test(s)\\n  - live debug event evidence\\n  - scenario replay.\\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\\n- First-failure depth is the top-priority gate.\\n  - Do not edit solver/collision runtime behavior until report includes:\\n    - `first_bad_frame`\\n    - `first_bad_substep_or_tick` (if available)\\n    - `first_bad_body_id` (from all dynamic bodies)\\n    - first-bad authoritative event fields (`debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt`)\\n    - exact runtime code path (file/function) for that first-bad transition.\\n  - If first-bad frame is `N`, diagnosis scope is locked to `{N-1, N, N+1}` until code-path attribution is complete.\\n  - Do not spend effort on later collapse frames before first-failure closure.\\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\\n\\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\\n\\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\\n  - `<emoji> <metric>: <delta% in backticks> (<old> -> <new>)`\\n- Only the percent is wrapped in backticks.\\n- Include one line per required metric and any newly added probes in the same style.\\n- Example:\\n  - 🎮 gpuFrameMs: `-21.02%` (21.6709 -> 17.1155)\\n  - 💥 collisionPipelineMs: `-36.24%` (13.0944 -> 8.3486)\\n  - 🗺️ bodyContactMapMs: `+0.42%` (0.3115 -> 0.3128)\\n  - 🔧 postCollisionMs: `-1.43%` (8.6412 -> 8.5180)\\n  - 🧮 solverTailMs: `-1.65%` (8.2626 -> 8.1267)\\n- Do not output tables in this context.\\n\\n## Architecture - Moving Parts (Quick Orientation)\\n- Runtime orchestrator:\\n  - `GPUPhysicsWorld::Step` records fixed-slot substeps, manages GPU budget update/finalize, and enqueues async readbacks.\\n- Slot gating:\\n  - `PrepareSlotArgs.hlsl` writes indirect dispatch args so inactive slots are true no-ops.\\n- Clock/budget:\\n  - `PhysicsClockUpdate.hlsl` computes requested/budgeted ticks.\\n  - `PhysicsClockFinalize.hlsl` publishes executed ticks + sim time.\\n- Collision pipeline:\\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\\n- Solver pipeline:\\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\\n  - Sign conventions and stiffness policy are critical.\\n- Observability:\\n  - Live debug (`AVBD_LIVE_DEBUG`) writes GPU event streams to `Debug/live/...`.\\n  - Snapshot rings expose coherent N-1 state via `TryGetLatestSnapshot`.\\n  - GPU timing (`AVBD_GPU_TIMING`) emits phase timing JSONL.\\n\\n## Debugging Reference Documents\\n- Primary process guide: `TESTING_PROCEDURE.md`\\n- Cross-investigation architecture + pitfalls: `GENERAL_KNOWLEDGE.md`\\n- Live debug contract/spec:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/GPU_Live_Debug_Pipeline_Spec_2026-02-17.md`\\n- Key investigation exemplars:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Offcenter_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Random30_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n\\n## Mandatory Skill Invocation\\n- For any scenario investigation, instability diagnosis, profiling pass, or scenario rerun workflow, invoke the `gpudebug` skill and follow it strictly end-to-end.\\n\\n## Common Debugging Pitfalls (Do Not Repeat)\\n- Using non-authoritative signals for root cause:\\n  - snapshots (`frame_*.json`) alone are insufficient for phase attribution.\\n- Skipping first-failure localization:\\n  - always find first bad frame/tick before implementation edits.\\n- Collision counter debug buffer bounds:\\n  - `collisionCountersByFrame.debugU32` exports only 64 u32 slots.\\n  - do not read/write indices beyond `[0..63]` in `DebugSystemFrame` event emitters.\\n- Probe plumbing errors:\\n  - validate SRV/UAV descriptors, register counts, and capture index ranges.\\n- Misreading runner outcome:\\n  - validate artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n- Scenario authoring mistakes:\\n  - keep YAML arrays inline where parser requires them.\\n\\n\\n## Skills\\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Build/Debug Postmortem\\n\\n## Postmortem Summary\\n- The main debugging failures came from using the wrong telemetry source.\\n  - `frame_*.json` is useful for state snapshots, but not authoritative for phase/perf diagnosis.\\n  - Use GPU live debug events under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*` for pipeline diagnosis.\\n- Temporary scenario generation caused false conclusions.\\n  - The YAML parser expects inline arrays (`[x, y, z]`) for many fields.\\n  - Block-style arrays can silently fall back to defaults (notably `half_extents`, capture arrays).\\n- Runner return code is currently unreliable for success/failure classification.\\n  - `run-scenario.ps1` may return non-zero even when the simulation reaches final frame and writes captures.\\n  - Always validate with run artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n\\n## Correct Build Procedure\\n- Release (fast runtime checks):\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1`\\n- Debug + live debug pipeline:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug`\\n- Debug + live debug + GPU timing:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug -gpuTiming`\\n\\n## Correct Run Procedure\\n- Canonical scenario run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\\\" -Config Release`\\n- No-render stress run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"<scenario>.yaml\\\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\\n- Always check:\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\\n\\n## Legacy Output Caveat\\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\\n\\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\\n- Known transient symptom:\\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\\n- Retry policy:\\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \\\"Write-Output interop_ok\\\"`\\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\\n\\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\\n- Use event files first:\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\\n- For histograms/summaries:\\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\\n\\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\\n\\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\\n\\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\\n\\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\\n- Update incrementally with:\\n  - commands run\\n  - artifact paths\\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\\n  - test evidence\\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\\n  - integration test(s)\\n  - live debug event evidence\\n  - scenario replay.\\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\\n- First-failure depth is the top-priority gate.\\n  - Do not edit solver/collision runtime behavior until report includes:\\n    - `first_bad_frame`\\n    - `first_bad_substep_or_tick` (if available)\\n    - `first_bad_body_id` (from all dynamic bodies)\\n    - first-bad authoritative event fields (`debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt`)\\n    - exact runtime code path (file/function) for that first-bad transition.\\n  - If first-bad frame is `N`, diagnosis scope is locked to `{N-1, N, N+1}` until code-path attribution is complete.\\n  - Do not spend effort on later collapse frames before first-failure closure.\\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\\n\\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\\n\\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\\n  - `<emoji> <metric>: <delta% in backticks> (<old> -> <new>)`\\n- Only the percent is wrapped in backticks.\\n- Include one line per required metric and any newly added probes in the same style.\\n- Example:\\n  - 🎮 gpuFrameMs: `-21.02%` (21.6709 -> 17.1155)\\n  - 💥 collisionPipelineMs: `-36.24%` (13.0944 -> 8.3486)\\n  - 🗺️ bodyContactMapMs: `+0.42%` (0.3115 -> 0.3128)\\n  - 🔧 postCollisionMs: `-1.43%` (8.6412 -> 8.5180)\\n  - 🧮 solverTailMs: `-1.65%` (8.2626 -> 8.1267)\\n- Do not output tables in this context.\\n\\n## Architecture - Moving Parts (Quick Orientation)\\n- Runtime orchestrator:\\n  - `GPUPhysicsWorld::Step` records fixed-slot substeps, manages GPU budget update/finalize, and enqueues async readbacks.\\n- Slot gating:\\n  - `PrepareSlotArgs.hlsl` writes indirect dispatch args so inactive slots are true no-ops.\\n- Clock/budget:\\n  - `PhysicsClockUpdate.hlsl` computes requested/budgeted ticks.\\n  - `PhysicsClockFinalize.hlsl` publishes executed ticks + sim time.\\n- Collision pipeline:\\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\\n- Solver pipeline:\\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\\n  - Sign conventions and stiffness policy are critical.\\n- Observability:\\n  - Live debug (`AVBD_LIVE_DEBUG`) writes GPU event streams to `Debug/live/...`.\\n  - Snapshot rings expose coherent N-1 state via `TryGetLatestSnapshot`.\\n  - Build/Debug Postmortem\\n\\n## Postmortem Summary\\n- The main debugging failures came from using the wrong telemetry source.\\n  - `frame_*.json` is useful for state snapshots, but not authoritative for phase/perf diagnosis.\\n  - Use GPU live debug events under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*` for pipeline diagnosis.\\n- Temporary scenario generation caused false conclusions.\\n  - The YAML parser expects inline arrays (`[x, y, z]`) for many fields.\\n  - Block-style arrays can silently fall back to defaults (notably `half_extents`, capture arrays).\\n- Runner return code is currently unreliable for success/failure classification.\\n  - `run-scenario.ps1` may return non-zero even when the simulation reaches final frame and writes captures.\\n  - Always validate with run artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n\\n## Correct Build Procedure\\n- Release (fast runtime checks):\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1`\\n- Debug + live debug pipeline:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug`\\n- Debug + live debug + GPU timing:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug -gpuTiming`\\n\\n## Correct Run Procedure\\n- Canonical scenario run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\\\" -Config Release`\\n- No-render stress run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"<scenario>.yaml\\\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\\n- Always check:\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\\n\\n## Legacy Output Caveat\\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\\n\\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\\n- Known transient symptom:\\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\\n- Retry policy:\\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \\\"Write-Output interop_ok\\\"`\\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\\n\\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\\n- Use event files first:\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\\n- For histograms/summaries:\\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\\n\\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\\n\\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\\n\\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\\n\\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\\n- Update incrementally with:\\n  - commands run\\n  - artifact paths\\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\\n  - test evidence\\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\\n  - integration test(s)\\n  - live debug event evidence\\n  - scenario replay.\\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\\n\\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\\n\\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\\n  - `<emoji> <metric>: <delta% in backticks> (<old> -> <new>)`\\n- Only the percent is wrapped in backticks.\\n- Include one line per required metric and any newly added probes in the same style.\\n- Example:\\n  - 🎮 gpuFrameMs: `-21.02%` (21.6709 -> 17.1155)\\n  - 💥 collisionPipelineMs: `-36.24%` (13.0944 -> 8.3486)\\n  - 🗺️ bodyContactMapMs: `+0.42%` (0.3115 -> 0.3128)\\n  - 🔧 postCollisionMs: `-1.43%` (8.6412 -> 8.5180)\\n  - 🧮 solverTailMs: `-1.65%` (8.2626 -> 8.1267)\\n- Do not output tables in this context.\\n\\n## Architecture - Moving Parts (Quick Orientation)\\n- Runtime orchestrator:\\n  - `GPUPhysicsWorld::Step` records fixed-slot substeps, manages GPU budget update/finalize, and enqueues async readbacks.\\n- Slot gating:\\n  - `PrepareSlotArgs.hlsl` writes indirect dispatch args so inactive slots are true no-ops.\\n- Clock/budget:\\n  - `PhysicsClockUpdate.hlsl` computes requested/budgeted ticks.\\n  - `PhysicsClockFinalize.hlsl` publishes executed ticks + sim time.\\n- Collision pipeline:\\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\\n- Solver pipeline:\\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\\n  - Sign conventions and stiffness policy are critical.\\n- Observability:\\n  - Live debug (`AVBD_LIVE_DEBUG`) writes GPU event streams to `Debug/live/...`.\\n  - Snapshot rings expose coherent N-1 state via `TryGetLatestSnapshot`.\\n  - GPU timing (`AVBD_GPU_TIMING`) emits phase timing JSONL.\\n\\n## Debugging Reference Documents\\n- Primary process guide: `TESTING_PROCEDURE.md`\\n- Cross-investigation architecture + pitfalls: `GENERAL_KNOWLEDGE.md`\\n- Live debug contract/spec:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/GPU_Live_Debug_Pipeline_Spec_2026-02-17.md`\\n- Key investigation exemplars:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Offcenter_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Random30_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n\\n## Mandatory Skill Invocation\\n- For any scenario investigation, instability diagnosis, profiling pass, or scenario rerun workflow, invoke the `gpudebug` skill and follow it strictly end-to-end.\\n\\n## Common Debugging Pitfalls (Do Not Repeat)\\n- Using non-authoritative signals for root cause:\\n  - snapshots (`frame_*.json`) alone are insufficient for phase attribution.\\n- Skipping first-failure localization:\\n  - always find first bad frame/tick before implementation edits.\\n- Collision counter debug buffer bounds:\\n  - `collisionCountersByFrame.debugU32` exports only 64 u32 slots.\\n  - do not read/write indices beyond `[0..63]` in `DebugSystemFrame` event emitters.\\n- Probe plumbing errors:\\n  - validate SRV/UAV descriptors, register counts, and capture index ranges.\\n- Misreading runner outcome:\\n  - validate artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n- Scenario authoring mistakes:\\n  - keep YAML arrays inline where parser requires them.\\n\\n\\n## Skills\\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. `WSL ... warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\\n\\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug`\\n- Debug + live debug + GPU timing:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./build.ps1 -debug -avbdDebug -liveDebug -gpuTiming`\\n\\n## Correct Run Procedure\\n- Canonical scenario run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"tests/massive_bench/scenario.yaml\\\" -Config Release`\\n- No-render stress run:\\n  - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ./run-scenario.ps1 -ScenarioPath \\\"<scenario>.yaml\\\" -Config Debug -NoRender -DebugMode live`\\n- Always check:\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/stdout.log` only for process/runtime diagnostics (startup/shutdown/errors), not physics counters.\\n  - `tmp/scenario_runs/<label>/<timestamp>/debug/frame_XXXX/events/*.txt` (when live debug build is used)\\n\\n## Legacy Output Caveat\\n- `stdout.log` physics counters (for example final `ContactCount`) are legacy/debug-print paths and are not authoritative.\\n- For contact/pair/phase counts, use only live debug event files under `debug/frame_XXXX/events/*`.\\n\\n## Windows Interop Reliability (WSL -> powershell/cmd)\\n- Treat Windows interop launch failures as potentially transient before changing code.\\n- Known transient symptom:\\n  - `WSL ... UtilAcceptVsock:271: accept4 failed 110`\\n- Retry policy:\\n  - retry the exact command at least 2-3 times first.\\n  - run a minimal sanity probe:\\n    - `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command \\\"Write-Output interop_ok\\\"`\\n  - only classify as environment-blocked if probe and retries keep failing.\\n- Do not infer engine regressions from this interop error class.\\n\\n## Performance/Phase Metrics - Source of Truth\\n- Use event files first:\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/global.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/PhysicsStep.txt`\\n  - `debug/frame_XXXX/events/CollisionPipeline.txt`\\n- For histograms/summaries:\\n  - `python3 tools/summarize_run_metrics.py <run_output_dir>`\\n- For GPU phase timing (p50/p95/p99):\\n  - Build with `-gpuTiming`.\\n  - Read JSONL timing stream from:\\n    - `Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/gpu_frame_segments.jsonl` (relative to process working dir; with runner this is typically under `build/bin/<Config>/Tests/_tmp/gpu_timing/`).\\n\\n## Reusable Stability Sweep Script\\n- For repeatable multi-scenario stability sweeps, use:\\n  - `python3 tools/integration_tests/scenario_stability_sweep.py --project-root . --config Debug --flags on --iterations 5 --stiffness 20,40,400 --output tmp/integration/results/scenario_stability_sweep_latest.json`\\n- Do not create new ad-hoc scripts for this same sweep; extend this script when new scenarios/metrics are needed.\\n\\n## Stability Objective (Commercial Priority)\\n- Primary target is to identify stiffness values/ranges that are stable and operationally usable.\\n- Full stability across the entire stiffness range is desirable but not a hard requirement.\\n- Commercially exploitable outcome is acceptable when rigid/high-stiffness simulation is stable, even if softer ranges are not fully robust yet.\\n- During iteration, prioritize mapping/expanding stable stiffness windows before attempting full-range guarantees.\\n\\n## Massive Bench Scenario Rules\\n- Use `procedural_spawn.count` (not `spawn.count`).\\n- Keep floor explicit and large:\\n  - `half_extents: [500, 0.5, 500]` (or scenario-specific justified value).\\n- For generated configs, keep arrays inline to avoid parser fallback.\\n\\n## Mandatory Debugging Discipline\\n- Maintain a working report in `Documentation/Reports/` for each investigation.\\n- Update incrementally with:\\n  - commands run\\n  - artifact paths\\n  - hypotheses + probability updates\\n  - test evidence\\n- Do not claim a fix from one signal; confirm on:\\n  - integration test(s)\\n  - live debug event evidence\\n  - scenario replay.\\n- First-failure localization must use all dynamic bodies from capture artifacts.\\n  - Do not infer first failure from the default tracked-body probe alone.\\n- If CPU-mirrored tests are encountered for solver/collision behavior, treat them as transitional only.\\n  - The goal is to replace/cover them with shader GPU contract tests that use real-world replay data from captured runs/events.\\n  - Prefer `UnitTest_*.hlsl` + `HlslTests` coverage with telemetry-derived values over synthetic CPU-only mirrors.\\n\\n## Paper Purity Rule (Mandatory)\\n- Implementation heuristics are strictly forbidden in solver/collision stability logic.\\n- Do not introduce or tune ad-hoc thresholds, growth gates, fudge factors, or fallback policies unless they are explicitly derived from the AVBD paper equations.\\n- If a paper value is not specified, keep behavior symbolic and equation-driven; do not invent constants.\\n- Any non-paper behavior must be removed or isolated behind an explicit non-default experimental flag, and must not be part of canonical runs.\\n- Examples of forbidden heuristic-only changes:\\n  - warm-start admissibility thresholds for normal/anchor/penetration matching,\\n  - penetration growth guards (for example `x * factor + bias`),\\n  - custom static/dynamic switching thresholds not defined by the paper.\\n\\n## Performance Report Output Format (Mandatory)\\n- If the operator asks to see perf, always use this exact bullet style:\\n  - `<emoji> <metric>: <delta% in backticks> (<old> -> <new>)`\\n- Only the percent is wrapped in backticks.\\n- Include one line per required metric and any newly added probes in the same style.\\n- Example:\\n  - 🎮 gpuFrameMs: `-21.02%` (21.6709 -> 17.1155)\\n  - 💥 collisionPipelineMs: `-36.24%` (13.0944 -> 8.3486)\\n  - 🗺️ bodyContactMapMs: `+0.42%` (0.3115 -> 0.3128)\\n  - 🔧 postCollisionMs: `-1.43%` (8.6412 -> 8.5180)\\n  - 🧮 solverTailMs: `-1.65%` (8.2626 -> 8.1267)\\n- Do not output tables in this context.\\n\\n## Architecture - Moving Parts (Quick Orientation)\\n- Runtime orchestrator:\\n  - `GPUPhysicsWorld::Step` records fixed-slot substeps, manages GPU budget update/finalize, and enqueues async readbacks.\\n- Slot gating:\\n  - `PrepareSlotArgs.hlsl` writes indirect dispatch args so inactive slots are true no-ops.\\n- Clock/budget:\\n  - `PhysicsClockUpdate.hlsl` computes requested/budgeted ticks.\\n  - `PhysicsClockFinalize.hlsl` publishes executed ticks + sim time.\\n- Collision pipeline:\\n  - Broadphase -> candidate pairs -> narrowphase/manifold -> contacts.\\n  - Contact quality (anchors/normals/penetration) is a primary stability determinant.\\n- Solver pipeline:\\n  - Cache initial error, iterative primal/dual updates, apply corrections, velocity.\\n  - Sign conventions and stiffness policy are critical.\\n- Observability:\\n  - Live debug (`AVBD_LIVE_DEBUG`) writes GPU event streams to `Debug/live/...`.\\n  - Snapshot rings expose coherent N-1 state via `TryGetLatestSnapshot`.\\n  - GPU timing (`AVBD_GPU_TIMING`) emits phase timing JSONL.\\n\\n## Debugging Reference Documents\\n- Primary process guide: `TESTING_PROCEDURE.md`\\n- Cross-investigation architecture + pitfalls: `GENERAL_KNOWLEDGE.md`\\n- Live debug contract/spec:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/GPU_Live_Debug_Pipeline_Spec_2026-02-17.md`\\n- Key investigation exemplars:\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Offcenter_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n  - `Documentation/Reports/Random30_Instability_Investigation.md`\\n\\n## Mandatory Skill Invocation\\n- For any scenario investigation, instability diagnosis, profiling pass, or scenario rerun workflow, invoke the `gpudebug` skill and follow it strictly end-to-end.\\n\\n## Common Debugging Pitfalls (Do Not Repeat)\\n- Using non-authoritative signals for root cause:\\n  - snapshots (`frame_*.json`) alone are insufficient for phase attribution.\\n- Skipping first-failure localization:\\n  - always find first bad frame/tick before implementation edits.\\n- Collision counter debug buffer bounds:\\n  - `collisionCountersByFrame.debugU32` exports only 64 u32 slots.\\n  - do not read/write indices beyond `[0..63]` in `DebugSystemFrame` event emitters.\\n- Probe plumbing errors:\\n  - validate SRV/UAV descriptors, register counts, and capture index ranges.\\n- Misreading runner outcome:\\n  - validate artifacts/logs, not exit code alone.\\n- Scenario authoring mistakes:\\n  - keep YAML arrays inline where parser requires them.\\n\\n\\n## Skills\\nA skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file.
